messages:
incidents-bot: 🚨 P1 pager: sustained GPU queue growth in prod-west (inference-west-1/gpu-pool-b). queue_length=640 (15m), avg_latency_tokens +120% over SLO. Auto-scaler attempted scale-up but no effective nodes added for 10m. Paging on-call now.
alice (oncall): ACK. I'm on it. Quick check: any customer-facing alerts already? tina?
tina (support): We have elevated latency alerts and some 502s to the API gateway. Support has two tickets from AcmeAI and BrightApps complaining of timeouts ~ 30m. Marking as P1 customer impact. I'll prepare comms template.
alice (oncall): ok. First goal: stop queue growth and identify why autoscaler didn't add capacity.
raj (infra): looking at autoscaler logs now. Seeing repeated failures: "scale-up failed: quota_exceeded: vGPU-allocations-per-account" and later "scale-loop disabled: safety_hotplug_storm_detected". Also seeing cloud API 429 spikes. Could be a quota throttle + driver instability causing terminated nodes.
lee (eng-runtime): adding runtime context. From node logs (tail of /var/log/syslog on flappy nodes):

```
Apr 28 10:12:03 gpu-17 kernel: NVRM: GPU 0000:af:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus.
Apr 28 10:12:03 gpu-17 kernel: docker: task killed due to OOM: pid=23456 name=worker
Apr 28 10:12:04 gpu-17 runtime: cuda: detected GPU fault cudaErrorIllegalAddress (err=77) on GPU0
Apr 28 10:12:05 gpu-17 runtime: driver: GPU reset required, rc=1
```

This is causing nodes to flake (kubelet restart, pod restarts) and the autoscaler sees nodes go NotReady and then fails allocation due to quota spikes.
marie (sre): Are these nodes all on the same driver build? We rolled driver 515->520 last week to the pool-b AMI.
lee (eng-runtime): Correct — pool-b AMI got the 520 rollout. I suspect an edge-case with that driver on this kernel version. We have previous infra notes about occasional "GPU has fallen off the bus" after noisy interrupts.
alice (oncall): plan of immediate mitigations (in order):
1) Throttle new requests at edge for non-paying tiers (reduce incoming RPS) — @tina please coordinate customer-facing rate-limits.
2) Temporarily increase autoscaler max for pool-b to allow burst to a separate pool if quota allows.
3) Spin up a temporary fallback pool (gpu-pool-fallback) using AMI with driver 515 (pre-rollout) in us-west region and attach routing.
4) Cordons/drain obviously flappy nodes, do not reboot in place.
5) If quota blocks scale-up, ask cloud for emergency vGPU quota bump (raj).

raj (infra): working on quota request now. Also starting provisioning of gpu-pool-fallback on older AMI (515). Kicking off with 10 nodes to start.

ops-bot: command output: `redwood-autoscaler set --pool inference-west-1/gpu-pool-b --max 80` -> accepted (old max 40). Note: cloud quotas still show allocation headroom only ~+12 vGPUs unless emergency quota granted.

lee (eng-runtime): I'm going to cordon/evict the worst offenders. Running: `kubectl get nodes -l pool=gpu-pool-b -o wide | grep NotReady\n` then `kubectl cordon gpu-17 && kubectl drain gpu-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30`. Output:

```
node/gpu-17 cordoned
evicting pod inference-worker-xyz... evicted
error: some pods failed to evict: kubelet restarting (retrying)
```

A few pods are stuck because kubelet is restarting rapidly; we'll force-cordon and isolate network to stop scheduling.
alice (oncall): good. lee, prioritize draining nodes that are causing OOM/KERNEL resets. Don't reboot; better to leave node out of rotation until infra confirms driver.
marie (sre): Metrics update @ +12m: queue_length down to 420 after partial throttling and early evictions, service latency still elevated for long-tail requests. Autoscaler shows 3 pending scale operations blocked by quota.
raj (infra): cloud support responded: emergency quota request submitted but ETA ~ 45-60m. They recommended scaling into a different family (a different instance type) which isn't currently in our AMI set — I can spin different instance types but need an AMI bake with driver 515 for it.
lee (eng-runtime): I'm starting a canary job on the fallback pool once nodes come up. Will run the same heavy model to validate. If fallback passes, we'll shift routing for a fraction of traffic to fallback pool.
tina (support): sent initial customer comms to AcmeAI and BrightApps (template: "we are experiencing degraded inference capacity in your region; mitigating steps underway; expect partial recovery within 60m; escalations open").
alice (oncall): update @ +27m: fallback pool nodes are initializing; cloud quotas still limited so we only got 8 up. I'm going to enable partial routing: 30% of new requests to fallback pool. Doing `redwood-router set-weight inference-west-1 --pool-fallback 30` now.
ops-bot: router change applied: 30% weight to gpu-pool-fallback. Confirmed.
lee (eng-runtime): canary run logs (excerpt):
```
canary-1: model load ok
canary-1: run 1 throughput = 65 tokens/s (baseline 72)
canary-1: no GPU resets observed in 10 runs
```
Good sign on older driver.
marie (sre): Observed reduction in GPU OOM errors on fallback pool traffic. Overall queue_length = 250. However node flaps still occur on ~6 nodes in pool-b.
raj (infra): I've isolated 6 nodes showing repeated kernel panics and set them to non-schedulable and flagged for host reprovision. Raising a change: reprovision these nodes to AMI with driver 515 but that will take ~90m.
alice (oncall): customer impact summary for handoff: AcmeAI, BrightApps, Tutorly saw timeouts / increased latency; estimated request failure rate peaked at ~6% globally in the region over the last 40m. Support has opened priority incidents. We're doing scheduled handoff in 30m window to infra+runtime for remediation and AMI rollback.
lee (eng-runtime): next steps for oncall handoff: continue cordon/drain of flappy nodes, validate fallback pool load, coordinate AMI rollback schedule with infra. I'll own postmortem and RCA for runtime driver mismatch.
raj (infra): I'll continue quota escalation and reprovision nodes. If quota doesn't arrive, plan B is to scale other regions and route traffic cross-region (latency tradeoff) — need approval from product for cross-region failover.
alice (oncall): handing off now to raj + lee for remediation and longer-term actions. I'll stay available for customer comms for the next 2 hours. Marie continue monitoring and update pager if regressions.
marie (sre): acknowledged. Setting alert thresholds to warn earlier and creating a follow-up ticket to validate driver compatibility in CI. Tagging @eng-runtime.
lee (eng-runtime): noted. Postmortem owner: lee. Tentative RCA scope: driver 520 vs kernel combo regression causing GPU resets -> node flaps -> autoscaler thrash -> quota exhaustion -> queue growth.
tina (support): I'll push an update to affected customers with ETA ~ 2h for full capacity recovery; linking support tickets to this incident thread.
incidents-bot: Incident transitioned to L2 (infra+runtime) for remediation. Handoff comment: "alice -> raj/lee; postmortem owner lee; support lead tina." Severity remains P1 until full capacity restored or all customers confirmed recovered.
alice (oncall): final note before leaving: please annotate all node reprovisions and autoscaler changes with `incident/3666600420` tag. If anyone needs to escalate to SEV board, ping me.
raj (infra): will do. continuing work.
lee (eng-runtime): continuing. will post recovery updates here.
marie (sre): monitoring window ongoing. next update in 30m or earlier on major changes."
